title: PRD: Define failure contracts and automated rollback acceptance tests for degraded serving paths
creator: Aisha Nader
description: Problem: Recent incidents revealed that certain degraded serving paths (KV cache thrash, quantization fallbacks, and kernel scheduling stalls) silently increase tail latency and token corruption without clear binary failures, which delays operator detection and rollback. Goal: Add explicit 'failure contracts' for degradable subsystems and ship automated acceptance tests that validate rollback behavior for canary and full rollouts. This PRD defines the contract, rollout gates, test matrix, and runbook acceptance criteria so that feature and runtime teams can ship with measurable rollback guarantees.
background: Postmortem CL-2025-01 identified three classes of degradations: 1) transient KV cache eviction storms that increase p99 latency; 2) aggressive quantization paths causing hallucination/regression on small prompt slices; 3) kernel mismatch fallbacks on certain GPU infra leading to token stream truncation. Current rollouts rely on manual telemetry review and ad-hoc runbooks. We need deterministic, automated rollback behavior and a set of acceptance tests that simulate each class and assert the controller will revert when the failure contract is violated.
requirements: Define a failure_contract schema: name, affected_layers, observable_metrics, failure_thresholds, detection_window, rollback_action

For each degradable serving path (kv-cache, quantization, kernel-fallback), specify observable metrics and thresholds. Example: kv-cache-storm -> p95 latency increase > 30% AND error_rate increase > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes
Extend rollout controller to accept failure_contract payloads and enforce automated rollback on contract breach
Provide a standardized canary test harness that can inject simulated faults (cache-evict, quantization-bitflip, kernel-timeout) and assert rollback behavior
Add unit and integration tests that run in CI and as part of preflight for runtime-related PRs
Publish operator runbooks and a post-decision timeline: detect -> notify -> auto-rollback -> post-rollback verification
Expose a console view for active failure_contracts and recent breach incidents with links to traces/dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Failure contract schema merged into runtime-config repo and documented in Confluence (docs link provided)
Rollout controller supports attaching failure_contracts to a deployment and will trigger automated rollback when thresholds are met (tested in staging)
At least three end-to-end chaos tests covering kv-cache eviction storm, quantization degradation, and kernel fallback are added to canary test suite and pass in CI
A simulated breach run in staging causes an automated rollback within the defined detection window and generates expected alerts and audit logs
Console shows contract status and recent breaches for the deployment under test
Operator runbook validated by on-call and runbook owner with a signed-off checklist
Performance regression guardrails: adding a failure_contract to a rollout is required for runtime code changes touching cache/quantization/kernel layers (enforced via PR checklist)
Telemetry: defined metrics (p50/p95/p99 latencies, request_error_rate, token_drop_rate, hallucination-proxy) are recorded and alerts created with documented thresholds
updates: 2025-02-11: Initial draft created after postmortem sync. Assigned to Luca for scoping.
2025-02-12: Eng feedback: request to split detection_window into short and long windows to reduce noise. Added to requirements.
2025-02-14: Design (DES-221) provided UI mocks for console contract view; moved mock links to Confluence.
2025-02-17: Devs estimated 8 points; identified ENG-4460 for canary harness work. Scheduled staging run for 2025-02-25.
2025-02-18: PM review complete; acceptance criteria updated to require operator sign-off and CI chaos tests.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter thresholds increase false-positive rollbacks. Plan to pilot conservative thresholds in staging and iterate with real traffic before enabling auto-rollback in production.

Rollback action types considered: immediate full rollback, traffic-split diversion to fallback model, and soft-degrade (reduce batch size). The PRD defaults to immediate rollback for high-customer-impact breaches.
Monitoring: need a lightweight 'breach-snapshot' artifact attached to the rollback event (trace id, sample requests, model version) for rapid RCA
Integration with SLO alerts is required; work will coordinate with SRE on alert deduping to avoid alert storms
